subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar permanently own an opt-in core hook contract that executes user-configured local commands from quota/provider events through shared config, GUI, and CLI surfaces?
rationale: The implementation can be mechanically repaired, but accepting a durable local command-execution API and its compatibility/security support burden is a product-boundary choice that code review cannot make safely.

options.title: Accept core hooks
options.body: Sponsor the opt-in hook contract after the argv round-trip defect is fixed and the trust/config behavior is documented as a supported interface.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Keep only a lower-level CLI or machine-readable event surface and defer GUI-managed command execution until the contract is smaller and easier to support.

options.title: Decline command execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observation-only and close the feature pair without adding a persistent external-command API.

recommendation.title: Accept core hooks
recommendation.body: Sponsor the opt-in hook contract after the argv round-trip defect is fixed and the trust/config behavior is documented as a supported interface.

likelyOwner.reason: As the repository owner, steipete is the clearest available owner for deciding whether this permanent core execution and configuration surface fits CodexBar.
